messages:
sara: Quick proposal: remove the freeform `user_agent` string from audit events and introduce a structured `client_meta` object + add `trace_id`. Reason: parsing and security masking are messy and we keep re-parsing UA to infer platform.

miguel: OK, high level - what fields in `client_meta`? and will this break customers?
paul: Suggested minimal shape: { client_meta: { name, version, platform }, trace_id }.
katie: +1 to structured. We need a compatibility plan for existing consumers who still depend on `user_agent` (esp partners ingesting raw events).
sara: Proposal: version audit payload to `audit_v2` in the event envelope. v1 stays as-is for 90 days. Server can emit both fields during the overlap: keep `user_agent` and add `client_meta` for now.
miguel: That seems safe. How will this affect KMS/PII handling? user_agent sometimes had IPs or tokens when clients misconfigured.
paul: We'll add a sanitizer on ingest that strips tokens from `user_agent` and any header-like content. For v2 we recommend clients populate `client_meta` correctly; server will stop writing `user_agent` after the deprecation window.
katie: Who owns the customer-facing notice? We should produce migration docs, example payloads, and a simple shim code snippet.
sara: I'll own the customer notification draft. Miguel/Platform to provide shim SDKs.
miguel: I'll add server-side feature flagging so we can enable dual-write per account for canary customers. Plan: opt-in dual-write, then auto-enable for everyone 2 weeks later, then remove `user_agent` after 90 days.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: staging rollout 2102480000, prod canary 2102500000 (permiguel).
paul: One more thing: RBAC and audit coverage. When we change schema, ensure RBAC logs (role assignments, token rotates) still emit the same logical fields (actor, action, target). client_meta is orthogonal but confirm our parsers ingest it.
katie: Also add a regression eval in Redwood Optimize: run prompts that exercise feature flags and confirm no missing trace_id in logs.
sara: Example event we'll publish in docs:
```json
{
  "envelope_version": "audit_v2",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-01T12:34:56Z",
  "actor": "user:alice@example.com",
  "action": "role.grant",
  "target": "team:research",
  "client_meta": { "name": "redwood-js-sdk", "version": "1.4.0", "platform": "node" },
  "trace_id": "01f3a9c2-...",
  "details": { "role": "admin" }
}
```
miguel: Nice. For customers using raw exports, we'll provide a short script to convert `user_agent` -> `client_meta` heuristically.
paul: Ops question: does this change require export schema bump for customers on Dedicated/Private? Answer: yes, we'll include migration guidance and a feature flag in Private so customers can preview.
katie: Action items:
- sara: draft customer notice + example JSON (due 2102469000)
- miguel: implement dual-write flag + shim SDKs (due 2102478000)
- paul: sanitize pipeline and add trace_id generation if missing (due 2102472000)
- katie: add regression eval and alert (due 2102476000)
sara: I'll create a short FAQ for common integrations (SIEMs, Splunk, Dataflow) and link converters.
miguel: If we see errors during canary, plan is immediate rollback to emit only `user_agent` (we'll keep the envelope_version header so consumers never get ambiguous schemas).
paul: tagging security: we should also log any PII that used to be in `user_agent` and surface to privacy for review.
katie: 👍 sounds good. Can we ship the notice end of day tomorrow?
sara: yes, aiming for that. I'll post the draft here once ready.
miguel: Thanks all. ping me if you want the feature-flag rollout doc now.
ops-bot: Reminder: weekly schema-change sync in #eng-security on Thursdays 16:00.
